name: rsv
title: Evaluation of Respiratory Illness in an Older Adult
description: Older adult with COPD presents with progressive cough, dyspnea, and low-grade fever after contact with sick grandchild. Covers RSV evaluation, differential diagnosis of acute respiratory illness, COPD exacerbation management, and hospitalization decision-making.
clinicalInvariants: Chief complaint: worsening cough and shortness of breath for 5 days, preceded by URI symptoms for 7 days
Conditions: COPD (mild-moderate, FEV1 65%), hypertension (controlled), BPH, former smoker (30 pack-years)
Medications: tiotropium daily, lisinopril 10mg daily, tamsulosin 0.4mg, albuterol PRN
Exposure: grandchild with 'bad cold' visited 10 days ago; no RSV or flu vaccination this season
Clinical findings: SpO2 93%, RR 22, temp 37.9C, bilateral wheezes, rhonchi, basilar crackles, prolonged expiratory phase
Assessment: likely RSV with COPD exacerbation; rule out bacterial pneumonia, influenza, COVID-19, heart failure
Management: RSV/flu/COVID testing, CXR, labs, increased bronchodilators, supportive care, low threshold for admission
Provider questions and SP responses remain substantively identical across all variants
